question: What does it mean if a protocol is stateless?

options.text: If a stateless protocol is used, it cannot be traced.
Server responds to a request, and then forgets about it
Client responds to server request and keeps track of the conversation.
If a protocol is stateless, it means it is unreliable

correctAnswerText: Server responds to a request, and then forgets about it
explanation: A stateless protocol (like HTTP) treats each request as an independent transaction unrelated to any previous request; the server processes the request and retains no session state about previous requests.

question: Which statement about Ethernet and Wi-Fi is false?

options.text: Both Wi-Fi and Ethernet support broadcast traffic.
Wireless LAN and Ethernet cannot coexist.
Wi-Fi and Ethernet both support unicast frames.
WLAN & Ethernet can use IP as their network layer protocol

correctAnswerText: Wireless LAN and Ethernet cannot coexist.
explanation: Wired Ethernet and Wi-Fi can coexist and can carry IP traffic on the same bridged LAN.

question: Which of the following statement about ICMP is FALSE?.

options.text: ICMP can report errors in IP packet delivery.
ICMP Time Exceeded can report an expired IPv4 TTL.
The echo-request and echo-reply messages test the connectivity between 2 systems
ICMP messages are not encapsulated in IP datagram

correctAnswerText: ICMP messages are not encapsulated in IP datagram
explanation: ICMPv4 messages are carried inside IPv4 packets, which identify ICMP with protocol number 1.

question: Which of the following is not part of IP header?
explanation: Correct option is (A) 'Window size'. This addresses the networking requirement in TCP/IP.

question: Which of these commands displays the IP address and MAC address mappings known to a windows system?
explanation: Correct option is (D) 'Arp   -a'. This addresses the networking requirement in IPv4 and IPv6.

question: Match the following with the corresponding protocols a) IP to host name resolution i) ICMP b) Accessing mail account ii) ARP c) Who owns IP address 172.16.1.2?  iii) DNS d) Destination unreachable          iv) IMAP
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i'. This addresses the networking requirement in NAT.

question: Which of the following statements is a true description of fiber Optic Cable.

options.text: Fiber optic cables transfer data in a mesh
Fiber optic cables are similar to coaxial cables
Fiber optic cables transfer data in light form
Fiber optic cable are similar to twisted pair cables

correctAnswerText: Fiber optic cables transfer data in light form
explanation: Fiber optic cables transmit data as pulses of light through thin strands of glass or plastic optical fibers, offering immense bandwidth and total immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

question: What is the maximum data field length (MTU) supported by the Ethernet?
explanation: Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) defines the maximum size of a packet or frame that can be sent in a single piece over a communication network without fragmentation. Standard Ethernet MTU is 1500 bytes (1518 bytes frame with header/FCS).

question: For which of the following is UDP unsuitable? Choose the most appropriate answer.
explanation: Correct option is (D) 'SMTP'. This addresses the networking requirement in DNS and DHCP.

question: The routing table of the router is shown below: Destination Subnet Mask Interface 192.168.43.0 255.255.255.0 eth0 192.168.43.0 255.255.255.128 eth1 192.12.17.5 255.255.255.255 eth3 Default eth2 On which interface will the router forward packets addressed to destinations 192.168.43.16 and 192.168.17.10
explanation: Routers use the Longest Prefix Match rule. Destination 192.168.43.16 matches 192.168.43.0/25 (eth1) because /25 is longer than /24. Destination 192.168.17.10 does not match any specific subnet and falls through to the Default route (eth2).

question: Which set of values uniquely identifies a TCP connection?

options.text: Sender IP & Sender Port, Receiver IP & Receiver Port
Sender MAC & Sender IP, Receiver MAC & Receiver IP

correctAnswerText: Sender IP & Sender Port, Receiver IP & Receiver Port
explanation: A TCP connection is identified by the two endpoints: source IP and port, plus destination IP and port.

question: Which of this IEEE standard defines Token Ring?
explanation: Correct option is (D) '802.5'. This addresses the networking requirement in Wireless Networks.

question: Which type of Packet (or Address) is not supported in IPV6?
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'Broadcast'. This addresses the networking requirement in IPv4 and IPv6.

question: Match the following i.  UTP 1. RJ11 ii. Serial Interface 2. RJ45 iii.Telephone 3. V.35
explanation: Correct option is (B) 'UTP-RJ45,Serial I/F – V.35, Telephone – RJ11'. This addresses the networking requirement in WAN.

question: After a host name is resolved to an IP address, what does a local host need to do next to communicate with the target host if the target host resides on the same subnet?

options.text: Resolve the IP address to physical address using ARP
Resolve the IP address to physical address using RARP
Send the packet to the default Router

correctAnswerText: Resolve the IP address to physical address using ARP
explanation: Correct option is (A) 'Resolve the IP address to physical address using ARP'. This addresses the networking requirement in Subnetting.

question: A hub connects 24 computers. A sends an Ethernet frame to B. Which computers receive the repeated signal from the hub?

options.text: Only A and B will receive
All computers except A will receive

correctAnswerText: All computers except A will receive
explanation: A hub repeats the signal onto all ports except the incoming port, so the other 23 computers see it. B accepts the frame addressed to it.

question: Which type of NAT creates a fixed one-to-one mapping between a private IP address and a public IP address?
explanation: Static NAT creates a fixed one-to-one mapping between a private IP address and a public IP address.

question: When a client opens a new TCP connection to a web server, which flag is set in its first TCP segment?
explanation: The initiating client sends SYN to start the TCP three-way handshake.

question: Which statement is false about a default single-VLAN Ethernet switch?

options.text: All the computers connected to a switch are in a same broadcast domain
Each port of a switch is a different broadcast domain
The switch learns MAC table entries from source MAC addresses.
Each port of a switch is a different collision domain

correctAnswerText: Each port of a switch is a different broadcast domain
explanation: By default, all access ports belong to the same VLAN and broadcast domain. The switch learns from source MAC addresses and uses destination MAC addresses to forward frames.

question: Which of this device stops MAC address broadcasts and thus separates two broadcast domains?
explanation: Correct option is (D) 'Router'. This addresses the networking requirement in Routing.

question: A computer is given an IP address as 192.168.100.35 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.224. Which of this IP address is not in the same IP subnet as this computer?
explanation: Correct option is (D) '192.168.100.65'. This addresses the networking requirement in Subnetting.

question: What will be the broadcast address for the network 10.10.0.0 with subnet mask 255.255.0.0?
explanation: Correct option is (C) '10.10.255.255'. This addresses the networking requirement in Subnetting.

question: What is the correct representation of following IPV6 address 3ffe:3700:0200:00ff:0000:0000:0000:0001?
explanation: Correct option is (B) '3ffe:3700:200:ff::1'. This addresses the networking requirement in IPv4 and IPv6.

question: Assume you are working on a PC and you are typing www.somesite.in . but you are not able to connect to it, but when you try 202.141.151.33 you are able to connect. What might be wrong? (assuming IP address of www.somesite.in is 202.141.151.33)

options.text: The company firewall restricts the access to websites
A virus could have caused the problem
The DNS server or DNS settings are not properly configured
The PC is configured to accept only IP address

correctAnswerText: The DNS server or DNS settings are not properly configured
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'The DNS server or DNS settings are not properly configured'. This addresses the networking requirement in DNS and DHCP.

question: Which OS command shows the routing table of the machine?

options.text: systems does not have the routing tables only routers have the routing tables

explanation: Correct option is (B) 'netstat –r'. This addresses the networking requirement in Routing.

question: Correctly match the "Layer Name" with the "Name of the unit exchanged" at that Layer. A) Physical layer i) Packet B) Data link layer ii) TPDU C) Network Layer iii) Bit D) Transport Layer               iv) Frame

options.text: A- iii, B- i, C-ii, D-iv
A- iii, B- iv, C- ii, D- i
A - iii, B - iv, C - i, D – ii

correctAnswerText: A - iii, B - iv, C - i, D – ii
explanation: Correct option is (D) 'A - iii, B - iv, C - i, D – ii'. This addresses the networking requirement in TCP/IP.

question: Which of this is a routed protocol?
explanation: Correct option is (A) 'IP'. This addresses the networking requirement in Routing.

question: Which of the following is the issue NOT addressed by the IP protocol at Network Layer.
explanation: Correct option is (D) 'Circuit setup'. This addresses the networking requirement in Subnetting.

question: Which of the OSI layers defines encryption technologies to protect transmitted data?
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'Presentation Layer'. This addresses the networking requirement in Network Security.

question: Which all transport layer header flags are involved while establishing a connection?
explanation: Correct option is (B) 'SYN and ACK'. This addresses the networking requirement in TCP/IP.

question: FTP at the Application Layer, TCP at the Transport Layer, IP at the Network Layer and 802.3 at the Data Link Layer would be representing a system in ___
explanation: Correct option is (A) 'LAN'. This addresses the networking requirement in Wireless Networks.

question: Which TCP/IP layer attaches a header and trailer to the transmitting data?
explanation: Correct option is (B) 'Data Link Layer'. This addresses the networking requirement in TCP/IP.

question: What is the principle difference between CDMA and GSM?

options.text: GSM and CDMA use the same technology but difference is in the handset
GSM uses TDMA while CDMA uses Spread Spectrum modulation
GSM phones can be used with CDMA , but the other way around is not possible
CDMA uses TDM While GSM uses FDM

correctAnswerText: GSM uses TDMA while CDMA uses Spread Spectrum modulation
explanation: Correct option is (B) 'GSM uses TDMA while CDMA uses Spread Spectrum modulation'. This addresses the networking requirement in Networking Protocols.

question: Which of the following is FALSE for VLANs?

options.text: Segmented by  port or MAC address
No routing is needed for connectivity between VLANS

correctAnswerText: No routing is needed for connectivity between VLANS
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'No routing is needed for connectivity between VLANS'. This addresses the networking requirement in VLAN.

question: ___in Example of Physical Address and __ is an example of  logical  address
explanation: Correct option is (C) 'MAC address, IP Address'. This addresses the networking requirement in IPv4 and IPv6.

question: Which of the following statement is not true related to Multi-mode Fiber optic cable?

options.text: It suffers a lot from high dispersion and attenuation rates.
It is used for short distance communication.
It uses a large diameter fiber optic core.
It has very low dispersion and attenuation rates.

correctAnswerText: It has very low dispersion and attenuation rates.
explanation: Fiber optic cables transmit data as pulses of light through thin strands of glass or plastic optical fibers, offering immense bandwidth and total immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

question: Which of the Wireless standard works only on 5GHz band?
explanation: Correct option is (A) '802.11a'. This addresses the networking requirement in Wireless Networks.

question: Which legacy Cisco IOS command sets the enable password in global configuration mode?
explanation: The enable password command is entered in global configuration mode. The enable secret command is the separate hashed-credential configuration.

question: An inbound ACL denies TCP and UDP ports 21, 23 and 25, then explicitly permits all other traffic. Which listed protocol can use its default port?
explanation: HTTP normally uses TCP port 80, so an ACL that denies only ports 21, 23 and 25 still allows it when other traffic is explicitly permitted.

question: If a PC does not have network connectivity to a router, which router port can be used to establish communication?
explanation: Correct option is (B) 'Console'. This addresses the networking requirement in Routing.

question: What is the maximum network-layer packet size a link can carry without fragmentation called?
explanation: The MTU gives the largest network-layer packet the link can carry without fragmentation.

question: Which IPv4 header field does traceroute use to discover successive hops?
explanation: Traceroute varies the IPv4 TTL so successive routers return ICMP Time Exceeded messages.

question: Which Windows command can release and renew a DHCP-assigned IPv4 address?
explanation: On Windows, ipconfig /release releases a DHCP lease and ipconfig /renew requests a new lease.

question: Which of the following command allows you to view the IP address and MAC address mapping that the computer has learned over the network?
explanation: The ARP cache stores IPv4-to-MAC mappings. On Windows, arp -a displays them.

question: Which of the following cable can be used for long distance reliable connectivity?
explanation: Single-mode fiber supports longer link distances than multimode fiber or twisted-pair copper.

question: Which of the following statement is true about the STP cable?

options.text: It can be used for a distance more than 100 meters.
supports more throughput as it has more cores than UTP
It is less affected by the Electro Magnetic Interference than UTP
It uses Infrared light for data transmission.

correctAnswerText: It is less affected by the Electro Magnetic Interference than UTP
explanation: Shielding helps reduce electromagnetic interference in twisted-pair cabling.

question: Which of the following OSI layer states the requirement of an address like the MAC address?
explanation: MAC addresses identify interfaces for frame delivery at the data link layer.

question: Which of the following OSI layer works to provide host to host reliable data transfer?
explanation: The transport layer can provide end-to-end reliability through a protocol such as TCP.

question: Which of the following OSI layer is not mapped by the Application layer of the TCP/IP model?
explanation: The TCP/IP application layer covers the OSI application, presentation and session layers. The OSI network layer maps to the TCP/IP internet layer.

question: Which of the following function is provided by the data link layer in the Ethernet technology?
explanation: Ethernet uses its frame check sequence to detect corrupted frames.

question: Which ICMP message does the sending host transmit when it runs ping?
explanation: Ping sends an ICMP Echo Request. A responding host returns an Echo Reply.

question: Which device, in its multilayer form, can switch traffic at Layer 2 and route traffic at Layer 3?
explanation: A multilayer switch can forward Ethernet frames at Layer 2 and route IP packets at Layer 3.

question: What is the first field of an Ethernet MAC frame after the preamble and start-frame delimiter?
explanation: The first field of the Ethernet MAC frame is the destination MAC address.

question: What is the nominal line rate of Fast Ethernet?
explanation: Fast Ethernet denotes 100 Mb/s Ethernet, such as 100BASE-TX. Some ports also negotiate 10 Mb/s for compatibility.

question: What is the maximum standard untagged Ethernet frame size, including the FCS and excluding the preamble?
explanation: An untagged Ethernet frame with a 1500-byte payload, 14-byte header and 4-byte FCS is 1518 bytes.

question: Which of the following technology is defined by the IEEE 802.5 specification?
explanation: IEEE 802.5 specifies Token Ring.

question: What was the higher of the two classic twisted-pair Token Ring rates?
explanation: Classic Token Ring installations used 4 or 16 Mb/s. The higher of these two rates is 16 Mb/s.

question: Which of the following is the WAN protocol that supports authentication?
explanation: PPP supports peer authentication through protocols such as PAP and CHAP.

question: Which of the following authentication protocol provides password security by not transmitting the actual password over the link?
explanation: CHAP verifies a challenge-dependent response derived from a shared secret without sending the secret itself.

question: Which of the following protocol allows you to trap particular events taking place on a system and send them to a central monitor system?
explanation: An SNMP agent can send a trap notification to a monitoring system when an event occurs.

question: Which of the following protocol is used by the devices to send error messages regarding the communication to the source?
explanation: ICMP carries IP-related errors back toward the sender, such as Destination Unreachable or Time Exceeded.

question: Which of the following Wi-Fi security option makes use of RADIUS server to provide additional security?
explanation: WPA-Enterprise uses 802.1X, commonly backed by a RADIUS authentication server.

question: What is the length of the IPV6 address?
explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long.

question: What IPv6 interface identifier does Modified EUI-64 derive from MAC address 00-02-4A-57-6B-73?
explanation: Insert FF:FE between the MAC address halves and flip the universal/local bit in the first octet. 00 becomes 02, yielding 0202:4AFF:FE57:6B73.

question: Which IEEE 802.11 amendment specifically introduced MAC-layer quality-of-service mechanisms for traffic such as voice and video?
explanation: IEEE 802.11e introduced MAC-layer quality-of-service mechanisms that help prioritize delay-sensitive voice and video traffic.

question: What will be the subnet mask if 18 bits are reserved for the network addressing?
explanation: Eighteen leading one bits give 255.255.192.0.

question: Which of the following NAT option allows multiple LAN clients to use same public IP address to access internet?
explanation: NAT overload uses port translation to let several internal hosts share one public IPv4 address.

question: How many usable host addresses are in an IPv4 /19 subnet?
explanation: A /19 leaves 13 host bits, giving 8,192 addresses. Excluding the network and broadcast addresses leaves 8,190 usable host addresses.

question: Which of the following is the broadcast address for a network address and subnet mask combination of 192.168.10.0 / 255.255.255.240?
explanation: A /28 contains 16 addresses. The 192.168.10.0 subnet ends at 192.168.10.15, its broadcast address.

question: You configure RIP to exchange routes for variable-length IPv4 subnets. Which configuration could explain why the subnet routes are missing or incorrect?

options.text: You forgot to enter static routes
RIP is not a routing protocol

explanation: RIPv1 omits subnet masks from routing updates, so it cannot advertise variable-length subnet masks. RIPv2 includes subnet masks.

question: What is the default administrative distance for OSPF?
explanation: Cisco routers assign OSPF routes a default administrative distance of 110.

question: Which of the following protocol does not supports Variable Length Subnet mask?
explanation: IGRP is classful and does not advertise subnet masks. EIGRP, OSPF and RIPv2 support VLSM.

question: Which of the following header field of the IP protocol is reduced by 1 by each router before forwarding the IP packet?
explanation: IPv4 routers decrement TTL by at least one before forwarding, discarding a packet if its TTL expires.

question: Which IPv4 flag is set by classic Path MTU Discovery?
explanation: Classic IPv4 Path MTU Discovery sets the DF flag so a router that cannot forward a packet without fragmentation returns an ICMP error.

question: Which of the following ICMP packet type is used by the routers to inform source when the TTL value in the packet becomes zero.
explanation: ICMPv4 type 11 is Time Exceeded. Code 0 indicates that TTL expired in transit.

question: Which of the following protocol on manageable switches helps to avoid switching loops?
explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol prevents Layer 2 forwarding loops by blocking redundant paths as needed.

question: Which of the following protocol helps admin replicate the VLAN information across multiple switches within the network?
explanation: Cisco VLAN Trunking Protocol distributes VLAN configuration across participating switches in a VTP domain.

question: How many collision domains are created by a HUB?
explanation: All ports on a shared Ethernet hub belong to one collision domain.

question: How many broadcast domains will be created by a 24 port switch with the default configuration?
explanation: With all 24 ports in one VLAN and no Layer 3 separation, the switch has one broadcast domain.

question: Which function occurs at Layer 2 of the OSI model?
explanation: Ethernet uses physical MAC addresses at the data link layer.

question: A technician is asked to secure the privileged EXEC mode of a switch by requiring a password. Which type of password would require this login and be considered the most secure?
explanation: The enable secret command sets a hashed credential for privileged EXEC access.

question: Which OSI layer does IP rely on to determine whether packets have been lost and to request retransmission?
explanation: A reliable transport protocol such as TCP detects missing data and requests retransmission.

question: When connectionless protocols are implemented at the lower layers of the OSI model, what is usually used to acknowledge that the data was received and to request the retransmission of missing data?

options.text: an upper-layer, connection-oriented protocol or service

correctAnswerText: an upper-layer, connection-oriented protocol or service
explanation: A connection-oriented higher-layer protocol can acknowledge received data and trigger retransmission of missing data.

question: What is the most specific subnet mask that allows at least 2,040 usable host addresses per subnet on 10.0.0.0?
explanation: A /21 leaves 11 host bits for 2,046 usable IPv4 host addresses. A /22 provides only 1,022.

question: Which statement is true about the TTL value of an IPv4 packet?

options.text: It determines the priority of a packet.
It specifies the remaining “life” of the packet.
It indicates that the packet has been fragmented.
It denotes the data payload type that the packet is carrying.

correctAnswerText: It specifies the remaining “life” of the packet.
explanation: TTL limits how long an IPv4 packet can circulate. Each router decrements it before forwarding.

question: What type of network is maintained if a server takes no dedicated role in the network?
explanation: In a peer-to-peer network, peers can both request and provide resources without a dedicated server.

question: A routing issue has occurred in your internetwork. Which of the following type of devices should be examined to isolate this error?
explanation: Routers forward packets between IP networks and are the devices to check for an inter-network routing issue.

question: A user sees the command prompt: Router(config-if)#. What task can be performed at this mode?
explanation: Router(config-if)# is the interface configuration prompt, used to configure the selected interface.

question: What information can be gathered by using the command netstat?
explanation: Netstat can show active TCP connections and their local and remote endpoints.

question: How can ARP be used to help document the network?

options.text: It can list each hop on the way to a destination host.
It can show the average latency of hosts on the network.
It can provide a list of physical addresses on the network.
It can indicate which hosts are not responding to network traffic.

correctAnswerText: It can provide a list of physical addresses on the network.
explanation: The ARP cache shows IPv4 addresses and corresponding MAC addresses learned on the local link.

question: What is the protocol data unit that is associated with the data link layer of the OSI reference model?
explanation: A frame is the data link layer protocol data unit.

question: Which application layer protocol allows administrators to log into a server from remote locations and control a server as though logged in locally?
explanation: Telnet provides an interactive remote terminal session. It is the remote login protocol among these choices.

question: Which statement identifies the DNS protocol?

options.text: It transmits information using TCP port 25.
It transfers and conveys information using HTML pages.
It matches a resource name with the required network address.
It requests and assigns an IP address, default gateway, and server addresses to hosts.

correctAnswerText: It matches a resource name with the required network address.
explanation: DNS resolves names to records, including A and AAAA records for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

question: With Cisco IOS VTY line-password authentication enabled, which password is used to establish a Telnet session?
explanation: Cisco IOS virtual terminal (VTY) lines handle remote Telnet sessions. A line password applies when line-password authentication is configured.

question: Which identifier is contained in the header of the Layer 2 Ethernet frame?
explanation: The Ethernet header carries both source and destination MAC addresses.

question: An IPv4 host needs to send an Ethernet frame to a host on the same subnet and has no ARP entry for it. What does it do?

options.text: The node sends out a Layer 3 broadcast message.
The node sends a message directly to the router for the address.
The node sends out an ARP request with the destination IP address.

correctAnswerText: The node sends out an ARP request with the destination IP address.
explanation: For a destination on the same IPv4 subnet, the sender broadcasts an ARP request to learn the destination host’s MAC address.

question: An administrator makes changes to the default configuration of a router and saves them to NVRAM. After testing, it is discovered that the configurations did not have the desired effect and must be removed. What steps must be taken to remove the changes and return the router to the default configuration?

options.text: Use no version of the commands that are issued.
Issue the erase startup-config command, and then reboot the router.
Issue the erase running-config command, and then reboot the router.

correctAnswerText: Issue the erase startup-config command, and then reboot the router.
explanation: Erasing the startup configuration removes the saved settings. A reload without saving the running configuration restarts the device without those settings.

question: A network administrator is tasked with connecting two workgroups that are configured to use different subnets. Which device should be selected to allow connectivity between users on the two networks?
explanation: A router forwards traffic between IP subnets.

question: Which program can be used to accomplish terminal emulation for configuring a router from the CLI through the console port?
explanation: HyperTerminal is a terminal emulator that can open a serial session through the router’s console port.

question: Which statement accurately describes file sharing in a peer-to-peer network?

options.text: Files are typically stored on the most powerful peer in the network.
Peers can either make requests, or respond to requests, but not both.

explanation: Peers share files directly and can manage access to their own resources without a dedicated file server.

question: Which broad function of the Ethernet MAC sublayer includes frame delimiting and error detection?
explanation: The MAC sublayer handles data encapsulation, including frame delimiting, MAC addressing and error detection.

question: Which router configuration mode would an administrator use to configure the router for SSH or Telnet login access?
explanation: Remote terminal access is configured under virtual terminal lines in line configuration mode.

question: What purpose does a hostname serve on a router?

options.text: uniquely identifies a router on the internet
used by routing protocols to identify peer routers
provides device identification to users logging on remotely
determines the hosts that are allowed to connect to the device

correctAnswerText: provides device identification to users logging on remotely
explanation: A hostname identifies the device to administrators and normally appears in the device prompt.

question: Which prompt is associated with the privileged exec mode?
explanation: The # suffix in R1# identifies privileged EXEC mode. The > suffix identifies user EXEC mode.

question: A technician wishes to connect two computers to move data from one to the other before reloading the operating system. The NICs on both PCs do not support autosensing feature. Which procedure will satisfy the requirement?

options.text: Interconnect the two PCs with a rollover cable.
Interconnect the two PCs with two rollover cables and a hub.
Interconnect the two PCs with a crossover cable.
Interconnect the two PCs with two crossover cables and a hub.

correctAnswerText: Interconnect the two PCs with a crossover cable.
explanation: A crossover cable connects the transmit and receive pairs of the two older NICs directly when they lack auto-MDI-X.

question: Two routers are connected via their serial ports in a lab environment. The routers are configured with valid IP addresses, but they cannot ping each other. The show interface serial0/0 command shows that the serial0/0 interface is up but the line protocol is down. What could be the cause of this problem?

options.text: The no shutdown command has not been applied to the interfaces.
The clock rate command has not been entered on the DCE interface.
The interface timers are not cleared.
The Fast Ethernet interface is emulating a serial interface by assigning it a timing signal.

correctAnswerText: The clock rate command has not been entered on the DCE interface.
explanation: The interface can be physically up while the line protocol remains down if the DCE end of the serial link supplies no clock signal.

question: What is the full address range, including network and broadcast addresses, of 10.10.128.0 with subnet mask 255.255.224.0?
explanation: The /19 block covers third-octet values 128 through 159, inclusive. The first and last addresses are the network and broadcast addresses.

question: When must a router serial interface be configured with the clock rate command?

options.text: when the interface is functioning as a DTE device
when the interface timers have been cleared
when the connected DTE device is shut down
when the interface is functioning as a DCE device

correctAnswerText: when the interface is functioning as a DCE device
explanation: The DCE side supplies clocking for a back-to-back serial link.

question: Due to a security violation, the router passwords must be changed. What information can be learned from the following configuration entries? Router(config)# line vty 0 3 Router(config-line)# password c13c0 Router(config-line)# login

options.text: The entries specify three Telnet lines for remote access.
The entries specify four Telnet lines for remote access.
The entries set the console and Telnet password to “c13c0″.
Telnet access will be denied because the Telnet configuration is incomplete.

correctAnswerText: The entries specify four Telnet lines for remote access.
explanation: The VTY range 0 through 3 contains four lines. The password and login commands enable line-password checking on those lines.

question: Which Cisco IOS password setting stores a hash by default?
explanation: Cisco IOS stores the enable secret in hashed form.

question: Which prompt represents the appropriate mode used for the copy running-config startup-config command?
explanation: The # suffix with no configuration-mode qualifier is privileged EXEC, where the copy command runs.

question: Which part of the destination IP address is used to match a routing-table prefix?

options.text: the host portion of the IP address
the network portion of the IP address

correctAnswerText: the network portion of the IP address
explanation: The router matches the destination IP address against routing-table prefixes and forwards using the longest matching prefix.

question: Well-known services and applications use which range of TCP/UDP port numbers?
explanation: IANA assigns system ports in the range 0 to 1023. Port 0 is reserved.

question: Which IPv4 address is a subnet broadcast address?
explanation: A /26 subnet has 64 addresses, so 192.168.4.0/26 ends at the broadcast address 192.168.4.63.

question: Which statement is true about network layer addressing?

options.text: Network layer addressing is used by Ethernet switches to make forwarding decisions.
A portion of the address is used to identify the network.

correctAnswerText: A portion of the address is used to identify the network.
explanation: A Layer 3 address contains a network prefix. Routers use that prefix when selecting a route.

question: Which OSI layer addressing is required to route packets between two networks?
explanation: Routers forward packets between networks using Layer 3 addresses.

question: How many host addresses may be assigned when using the 128.107.0.0 network address with a subnet mask of 255.255.248.0?
explanation: A /21 leaves 11 host bits and has 2,048 total addresses. Removing the network and broadcast addresses leaves 2,046.

question: During the encapsulation process, what is the PDU of the internet layer?
explanation: The TCP/IP internet layer encapsulates data into an IP packet.

question: Which service is used when the nslookup command is issued on a computer?
explanation: Nslookup sends DNS queries to resolve names or inspect DNS records.

question: What are the default terminal emulation software settings when configuring a Cisco device through a console port?

question: What is the full address range, including network and broadcast addresses, of 10.10.128.0 with subnet mask 255.255.224.0?
explanation: The /19 block covers third-octet values 128 through 159, inclusive. The first and last addresses are the network and broadcast addresses.

question: When must a router serial interface be configured with the clock rate command?

options.text: when the interface is functioning as a DTE device
when the interface timers have been cleared
when the connected DTE device is shut down
when the interface is functioning as a DCE device

correctAnswerText: when the interface is functioning as a DCE device
explanation: The DCE side supplies clocking for a back-to-back serial link.

question: Due to a security violation, the router passwords must be changed. What information can be learned from the following configuration entries? Router(config)# line vty 0 3 Router(config-line)# password c13c0 Router(config-line)# login

options.text: The entries specify three Telnet lines for remote access.
The entries specify four Telnet lines for remote access.
The entries set the console and Telnet password to “c13c0″.
Telnet access will be denied because the Telnet configuration is incomplete.

correctAnswerText: The entries specify four Telnet lines for remote access.
explanation: The VTY range 0 through 3 contains four lines. The password and login commands enable line-password checking on those lines.

question: Which Cisco IOS password setting stores a hash by default?
explanation: Cisco IOS stores the enable secret in hashed form.

question: Which prompt represents the appropriate mode used for the copy running-config startup-config command?
explanation: The # suffix with no configuration-mode qualifier is privileged EXEC, where the copy command runs.

question: Which part of the destination IP address is used to match a routing-table prefix?

options.text: the host portion of the IP address
the network portion of the IP address

correctAnswerText: the network portion of the IP address
explanation: The router matches the destination IP address against routing-table prefixes and forwards using the longest matching prefix.

question: Well-known services and applications use which range of TCP/UDP port numbers?
explanation: IANA assigns system ports in the range 0 to 1023. Port 0 is reserved.

question: Which IPv4 address is a subnet broadcast address?
explanation: A /26 subnet has 64 addresses, so 192.168.4.0/26 ends at the broadcast address 192.168.4.63.

question: Which statement is true about network layer addressing?

options.text: Network layer addressing is used by Ethernet switches to make forwarding decisions.
A portion of the address is used to identify the network.

correctAnswerText: A portion of the address is used to identify the network.
explanation: A Layer 3 address contains a network prefix. Routers use that prefix when selecting a route.

question: Which OSI layer addressing is required to route packets between two networks?
explanation: Routers forward packets between networks using Layer 3 addresses.

question: How many host addresses may be assigned when using the 128.107.0.0 network address with a subnet mask of 255.255.248.0?
explanation: A /21 leaves 11 host bits and has 2,048 total addresses. Removing the network and broadcast addresses leaves 2,046.

question: During the encapsulation process, what is the PDU of the internet layer?
explanation: The TCP/IP internet layer encapsulates data into an IP packet.

question: Which service is used when the nslookup command is issued on a computer?
explanation: Nslookup sends DNS queries to resolve names or inspect DNS records.

question: Which function occurs at Layer 2 of the OSI model?
explanation: Ethernet uses physical MAC addresses at the data link layer.

question: A technician is asked to secure the privileged EXEC mode of a switch by requiring a password. Which type of password would require this login and be considered the most secure?
explanation: The enable secret command sets a hashed credential for privileged EXEC access.

question: Which OSI layer does IP rely on to determine whether packets have been lost and to request retransmission?
explanation: A reliable transport protocol such as TCP detects missing data and requests retransmission.

question: When connectionless protocols are implemented at the lower layers of the OSI model, what is usually used to acknowledge that the data was received and to request the retransmission of missing data?

options.text: an upper-layer, connection-oriented protocol or service

correctAnswerText: an upper-layer, connection-oriented protocol or service
explanation: A connection-oriented higher-layer protocol can acknowledge received data and trigger retransmission of missing data.

question: What is the most specific subnet mask that allows at least 2,040 usable host addresses per subnet on 10.0.0.0?
explanation: A /21 leaves 11 host bits for 2,046 usable IPv4 host addresses. A /22 provides only 1,022.

question: Which statement is true about the TTL value of an IPv4 packet?

options.text: It determines the priority of a packet.
It specifies the remaining “life” of the packet.
It indicates that the packet has been fragmented.
It denotes the data payload type that the packet is carrying.

correctAnswerText: It specifies the remaining “life” of the packet.
explanation: TTL limits how long an IPv4 packet can circulate. Each router decrements it before forwarding.

question: What type of network is maintained if a server takes no dedicated role in the network?
explanation: In a peer-to-peer network, peers can both request and provide resources without a dedicated server.

question: A routing issue has occurred in your internetwork. Which of the following type of devices should be examined to isolate this error?
explanation: Routers forward packets between IP networks and are the devices to check for an inter-network routing issue.

question: A user sees the command prompt: Router(config-if)#. What task can be performed at this mode?
explanation: Router(config-if)# is the interface configuration prompt, used to configure the selected interface.

question: What information can be gathered by using the command netstat?
explanation: Netstat can show active TCP connections and their local and remote endpoints.

question: How can ARP be used to help document the network?

options.text: It can list each hop on the way to a destination host.
It can show the average latency of hosts on the network.
It can provide a list of physical addresses on the network.
It can indicate which hosts are not responding to network traffic.

correctAnswerText: It can provide a list of physical addresses on the network.
explanation: The ARP cache shows IPv4 addresses and corresponding MAC addresses learned on the local link.

question: What is the protocol data unit that is associated with the data link layer of the OSI reference model?
explanation: A frame is the data link layer protocol data unit.

question: Which application layer protocol allows administrators to log into a server from remote locations and control a server as though logged in locally?
explanation: Telnet provides an interactive remote terminal session. It is the remote login protocol among these choices.

question: Which statement identifies the DNS protocol?

options.text: It transmits information using TCP port 25.
It transfers and conveys information using HTML pages.
It matches a resource name with the required network address.
It requests and assigns an IP address, default gateway, and server addresses to hosts.

correctAnswerText: It matches a resource name with the required network address.
explanation: DNS resolves names to records, including A and AAAA records for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

question: With Cisco IOS VTY line-password authentication enabled, which password is used to establish a Telnet session?
explanation: Cisco IOS virtual terminal (VTY) lines handle remote Telnet sessions. A line password applies when line-password authentication is configured.

question: Which identifier is contained in the header of the Layer 2 Ethernet frame?
explanation: The Ethernet header carries both source and destination MAC addresses.

question: An IPv4 host needs to send an Ethernet frame to a host on the same subnet and has no ARP entry for it. What does it do?

options.text: The node sends out a Layer 3 broadcast message.
The node sends a message directly to the router for the address.
The node sends out an ARP request with the destination IP address.

correctAnswerText: The node sends out an ARP request with the destination IP address.
explanation: For a destination on the same IPv4 subnet, the sender broadcasts an ARP request to learn the destination host’s MAC address.

question: An administrator makes changes to the default configuration of a router and saves them to NVRAM. After testing, it is discovered that the configurations did not have the desired effect and must be removed. What steps must be taken to remove the changes and return the router to the default configuration?

options.text: Use no version of the commands that are issued.
Issue the erase startup-config command, and then reboot the router.
Issue the erase running-config command, and then reboot the router.

correctAnswerText: Issue the erase startup-config command, and then reboot the router.
explanation: Erasing the startup configuration removes the saved settings. A reload without saving the running configuration restarts the device without those settings.

question: A network administrator is tasked with connecting two workgroups that are configured to use different subnets. Which device should be selected to allow connectivity between users on the two networks?
explanation: A router forwards traffic between IP subnets.

question: Which program can be used to accomplish terminal emulation for configuring a router from the CLI through the console port?
explanation: HyperTerminal is a terminal emulator that can open a serial session through the router’s console port.

question: Which statement accurately describes file sharing in a peer-to-peer network?

options.text: Files are typically stored on the most powerful peer in the network.
Peers can either make requests, or respond to requests, but not both.

explanation: Peers share files directly and can manage access to their own resources without a dedicated file server.

question: Which broad function of the Ethernet MAC sublayer includes frame delimiting and error detection?
explanation: The MAC sublayer handles data encapsulation, including frame delimiting, MAC addressing and error detection.

question: Which router configuration mode would an administrator use to configure the router for SSH or Telnet login access?
explanation: Remote terminal access is configured under virtual terminal lines in line configuration mode.

question: What purpose does a hostname serve on a router?

options.text: uniquely identifies a router on the internet
used by routing protocols to identify peer routers
provides device identification to users logging on remotely
determines the hosts that are allowed to connect to the device

correctAnswerText: provides device identification to users logging on remotely
explanation: A hostname identifies the device to administrators and normally appears in the device prompt.

question: Which prompt is associated with the privileged exec mode?
explanation: The # suffix in R1# identifies privileged EXEC mode. The > suffix identifies user EXEC mode.

question: A technician wishes to connect two computers to move data from one to the other before reloading the operating system. The NICs on both PCs do not support autosensing feature. Which procedure will satisfy the requirement?

options.text: Interconnect the two PCs with a rollover cable.
Interconnect the two PCs with two rollover cables and a hub.
Interconnect the two PCs with a crossover cable.
Interconnect the two PCs with two crossover cables and a hub.

correctAnswerText: Interconnect the two PCs with a crossover cable.
explanation: A crossover cable connects the transmit and receive pairs of the two older NICs directly when they lack auto-MDI-X.

question: Two routers are connected via their serial ports in a lab environment. The routers are configured with valid IP addresses, but they cannot ping each other. The show interface serial0/0 command shows that the serial0/0 interface is up but the line protocol is down. What could be the cause of this problem?

options.text: The no shutdown command has not been applied to the interfaces.
The clock rate command has not been entered on the DCE interface.
The interface timers are not cleared.
The Fast Ethernet interface is emulating a serial interface by assigning it a timing signal.

correctAnswerText: The clock rate command has not been entered on the DCE interface.
explanation: The interface can be physically up while the line protocol remains down if the DCE end of the serial link supplies no clock signal.

question: What is the maximum network-layer packet size a link can carry without fragmentation called?
explanation: The MTU gives the largest network-layer packet the link can carry without fragmentation.

question: Which IPv4 header field does traceroute use to discover successive hops?
explanation: Traceroute varies the IPv4 TTL so successive routers return ICMP Time Exceeded messages.

question: Which Windows command can release and renew a DHCP-assigned IPv4 address?
explanation: On Windows, ipconfig /release releases a DHCP lease and ipconfig /renew requests a new lease.

question: Which of the following command allows you to view the IP address and MAC address mapping that the computer has learned over the network?
explanation: The ARP cache stores IPv4-to-MAC mappings. On Windows, arp -a displays them.

question: Which of the following cable can be used for long distance reliable connectivity?
explanation: Single-mode fiber supports longer link distances than multimode fiber or twisted-pair copper.

question: Which of the following statement is true about the STP cable?

options.text: It can be used for a distance more than 100 meters.
supports more throughput as it has more cores than UTP
It is less affected by the Electro Magnetic Interference than UTP
It uses Infrared light for data transmission.

correctAnswerText: It is less affected by the Electro Magnetic Interference than UTP
explanation: Shielding helps reduce electromagnetic interference in twisted-pair cabling.

question: Which of the following OSI layer states the requirement of an address like the MAC address?
explanation: MAC addresses identify interfaces for frame delivery at the data link layer.

question: Which of the following OSI layer works to provide host to host reliable data transfer?
explanation: The transport layer can provide end-to-end reliability through a protocol such as TCP.

question: Which of the following OSI layer is not mapped by the Application layer of the TCP/IP model?
explanation: The TCP/IP application layer covers the OSI application, presentation and session layers. The OSI network layer maps to the TCP/IP internet layer.

question: Which of the following function is provided by the data link layer in the Ethernet technology?
explanation: Ethernet uses its frame check sequence to detect corrupted frames.

question: Which ICMP message does the sending host transmit when it runs ping?
explanation: Ping sends an ICMP Echo Request. A responding host returns an Echo Reply.

question: Which device, in its multilayer form, can switch traffic at Layer 2 and route traffic at Layer 3?
explanation: A multilayer switch can forward Ethernet frames at Layer 2 and route IP packets at Layer 3.

question: What is the first field of an Ethernet MAC frame after the preamble and start-frame delimiter?
explanation: The first field of the Ethernet MAC frame is the destination MAC address.

question: What is the nominal line rate of Fast Ethernet?
explanation: Fast Ethernet denotes 100 Mb/s Ethernet, such as 100BASE-TX. Some ports also negotiate 10 Mb/s for compatibility.

question: What is the maximum standard untagged Ethernet frame size, including the FCS and excluding the preamble?
explanation: An untagged Ethernet frame with a 1500-byte payload, 14-byte header and 4-byte FCS is 1518 bytes.

question: Which of the following technology is defined by the IEEE 802.5 specification?
explanation: IEEE 802.5 specifies Token Ring.

question: What was the higher of the two classic twisted-pair Token Ring rates?
explanation: Classic Token Ring installations used 4 or 16 Mb/s. The higher of these two rates is 16 Mb/s.

question: Which of the following is the WAN protocol that supports authentication?
explanation: PPP supports peer authentication through protocols such as PAP and CHAP.

question: Which of the following authentication protocol provides password security by not transmitting the actual password over the link?
explanation: CHAP verifies a challenge-dependent response derived from a shared secret without sending the secret itself.

question: Which of the following protocol allows you to trap particular events taking place on a system and send them to a central monitor system?
explanation: An SNMP agent can send a trap notification to a monitoring system when an event occurs.

question: Which of the following protocol is used by the devices to send error messages regarding the communication to the source?
explanation: ICMP carries IP-related errors back toward the sender, such as Destination Unreachable or Time Exceeded.

question: Which of the following Wi-Fi security option makes use of RADIUS server to provide additional security?
explanation: WPA-Enterprise uses 802.1X, commonly backed by a RADIUS authentication server.

question: What is the length of the IPV6 address?
explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long.

question: What IPv6 interface identifier does Modified EUI-64 derive from MAC address 00-02-4A-57-6B-73?
explanation: Insert FF:FE between the MAC address halves and flip the universal/local bit in the first octet. 00 becomes 02, yielding 0202:4AFF:FE57:6B73.

question: Which IEEE 802.11 amendment specifically introduced MAC-layer quality-of-service mechanisms for traffic such as voice and video?
explanation: IEEE 802.11e introduced MAC-layer quality-of-service mechanisms that help prioritize delay-sensitive voice and video traffic.

question: What will be the subnet mask if 18 bits are reserved for the network addressing?
explanation: Eighteen leading one bits give 255.255.192.0.

question: Which of the following NAT option allows multiple LAN clients to use same public IP address to access internet?
explanation: NAT overload uses port translation to let several internal hosts share one public IPv4 address.

question: How many usable host addresses are in an IPv4 /19 subnet?
explanation: A /19 leaves 13 host bits, giving 8,192 addresses. Excluding the network and broadcast addresses leaves 8,190 usable host addresses.

question: Which of the following is the broadcast address for a network address and subnet mask combination of 192.168.10.0 / 255.255.255.240?
explanation: A /28 contains 16 addresses. The 192.168.10.0 subnet ends at 192.168.10.15, its broadcast address.

question: You configure RIP to exchange routes for variable-length IPv4 subnets. Which configuration could explain why the subnet routes are missing or incorrect?

options.text: You forgot to enter static routes
RIP is not a routing protocol

explanation: RIPv1 omits subnet masks from routing updates, so it cannot advertise variable-length subnet masks. RIPv2 includes subnet masks.

question: What is the default administrative distance for OSPF?
explanation: Cisco routers assign OSPF routes a default administrative distance of 110.

question: Which of the following protocol does not supports Variable Length Subnet mask?
explanation: IGRP is classful and does not advertise subnet masks. EIGRP, OSPF and RIPv2 support VLSM.

question: Which of the following header field of the IP protocol is reduced by 1 by each router before forwarding the IP packet?
explanation: IPv4 routers decrement TTL by at least one before forwarding, discarding a packet if its TTL expires.

question: Which IPv4 flag is set by classic Path MTU Discovery?
explanation: Classic IPv4 Path MTU Discovery sets the DF flag so a router that cannot forward a packet without fragmentation returns an ICMP error.

question: Which of the following ICMP packet type is used by the routers to inform source when the TTL value in the packet becomes zero.
explanation: ICMPv4 type 11 is Time Exceeded. Code 0 indicates that TTL expired in transit.

question: Which of the following protocol on manageable switches helps to avoid switching loops?
explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol prevents Layer 2 forwarding loops by blocking redundant paths as needed.

question: Which of the following protocol helps admin replicate the VLAN information across multiple switches within the network?
explanation: Cisco VLAN Trunking Protocol distributes VLAN configuration across participating switches in a VTP domain.

question: How many collision domains are created by a HUB?
explanation: All ports on a shared Ethernet hub belong to one collision domain.

question: How many broadcast domains will be created by a 24 port switch with the default configuration?
explanation: With all 24 ports in one VLAN and no Layer 3 separation, the switch has one broadcast domain.

question: A lab host uses 10.44.19.173/27. What are the first and last usable host addresses in its subnet?
explanation: A /27 has blocks of 32 addresses. The block starts at .160 and broadcasts at .191, leaving .161 through .190 for hosts.

question: You are dividing 172.28.32.0/24 into fixed-size subnets. Each subnet needs at least 50 usable addresses. How many equal subnets fit using the smallest possible blocks?
explanation: A /26 provides 62 usable addresses. A /24 divides into four /26 blocks.

question: A router has matching routes for 10.70.0.0/16, 10.70.32.0/20 and 10.70.36.0/24. Which entry does it use for destination 10.70.39.18?
explanation: 10.70.39.18 falls within the /20’s third-octet range of 32 through 47. The /24 for 10.70.36.0 does not match.

question: A TCP receiver has a contiguous byte stream through sequence number 7999. It receives bytes 8500 through 8999 while bytes 8000 through 8499 are still missing. What cumulative ACK number does it send while the gap remains?
explanation: The cumulative ACK names the next contiguous byte expected. Selective acknowledgments can separately report out-of-order data.

question: A receiver advertises a TCP window of 6,000 bytes starting at sequence 25,000. The sender already has 4,500 unacknowledged bytes in that window. How many additional bytes fit in the advertised window, ignoring congestion control?
explanation: The advertised window accounts for bytes already in flight. Subtracting 4,500 from 6,000 leaves 1,500 bytes.

question: Two clients behind the same switch send traffic to a remote server. A router forwards each IPv4 packet without NAT. Which destination value changes when the router sends the packet over a different Ethernet link?
explanation: The router builds a new frame for the next link and uses the next hop’s MAC address. The IP destination remains the remote server.

question: A server with IPv6 prefix 2001:db8:427:9::/64 uses address 2001:db8:427:9::8. Which listed address shares its /64 prefix?
explanation: A /64 compares the first four 16-bit groups. They must be 2001:db8:427:9.

question: On one VLAN, a switch receives a unicast frame on port 3. It knows the source MAC but has no entry for the destination. What does it do under normal learning-switch behavior?

options.text: Sends it only back out of port 3
Drops it until ARP updates the switch’s MAC table
Floods it to forwarding ports in every VLAN
Floods it to the other forwarding ports in that VLAN

correctAnswerText: Floods it to the other forwarding ports in that VLAN
explanation: Unknown unicast is flooded within the originating VLAN, excluding the ingress port.

question: VLAN 40 works between access ports on the same switch. It fails between two switches even though VLAN 30 works across their trunk. Which trunk configuration should you check first?

options.text: Whether the access ports send every VLAN on the trunk
Whether the trunk is configured with an IP default route
Whether VLAN 40 is allowed on the trunk

correctAnswerText: Whether VLAN 40 is allowed on the trunk
explanation: An 802.1Q trunk forwards frames for allowed VLANs. A trunk carrying VLAN 30 can still omit VLAN 40.

question: Two internal clients open TCP connections from port 51000 to the same external IP and port. A NAT gateway uses one public IPv4 address for both. How can it keep the public-side TCP connections distinct?

options.text: Change both destination addresses to the internal gateway
Assign the same public-side 4-tuple to both connections
Use the source Ethernet MAC as a public-side TCP field

explanation: Port address translation can choose different public source ports so the public-side TCP tuples differ.

question: A recursive resolver cached a DNS A record for 300 seconds. After 120 seconds, an administrator changes the authoritative record. Without a manual cache flush, how much longer may the resolver normally serve its cached value?
explanation: The cache can use the existing answer until its original TTL expires. There are 300 minus 120 seconds remaining.

question: During initial DHCPv4 address assignment, a client receives offers from two servers. Which message normally announces the offer it has selected?
explanation: The client sends DHCPREQUEST, identifying the selected server and requesting the offered address. The server confirms with DHCPACK.

question: Two lab routers exchange IPv4 packets across PPP. The PPP link is authenticated, but IPv4 traffic is unavailable because IPv4 negotiation failed. Which PPP component should you inspect?
explanation: IPCP is the PPP network control protocol for IPv4. It negotiates IPv4 parameters after the link has been established.

question: A classroom has two nearby 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi access points using 20 MHz channels. One uses channel 1. Which listed channel avoids overlap with it in the common 1/6/11 plan?
explanation: Channels 1 and 6 have center frequencies 25 MHz apart and are part of the conventional non-overlapping 20 MHz plan.

question: A stateless inbound ACL checks two overlapping rules in order. Rule 1 permits all packets from 192.0.2.0/24. Rule 2 denies packets from 192.0.2.45. Under first-match processing, what happens to a packet from 192.0.2.45?

options.text: The ACL evaluates both rules and applies whichever was created last
Rule 1 permits it before rule 2 is reached
The rules cancel out and the implicit deny applies
Rule 2 denies it because it has a longer prefix

correctAnswerText: Rule 1 permits it before rule 2 is reached
explanation: The first matching ACL rule decides the outcome. Put the host-specific exception before the broader permit.
